Would you enjoy leading drug development for rare conditions? Are you a medic with experience designing clinical trials and interacting with regulatory authorities?

_If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Medical Director, Clinical Development, Endocrine & Rare Diseases

_

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking an energetic and passionate Medical Director to join our team. As a member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in driving the design, safety monitoring, and data analysis within the Endocrine and Rare Disease Medical Sciences area. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will join the Clinical Development team, being part of the Endocrine & Rare Disease Medical Sciences organization. You will report directly to the VP of Clinical Science who is based in the US. You will be based in Hellerup together with the Danish team.

Since you will join a team based in different time zones, you must be available for evening meetings. This position also may require occasional international travel.

Your key responsibilities will be

• Contribute to formulation and implementation of the Clinical Development Plan

• Leverage medical expertise and hands-on clinical experience to promote relevance and rigor of the development program

• For clinical trials: design, provide overall oversight, and support site and subject retention

• Serve as a Medical Monitor for clinical trials, ensure study integrity, and track accumulating safety and efficacy data

• Provide leadership to teams of medical monitors and study teams

• Ensure successful completion of trial-related documents (including clinical trial protocols, investigator brochures, medical monitoring plans, site training materials, clinical study reports, health authority responses, standard operating procedures, etc.) with cross-functional team members

• Ensure study integrity, and track accumulating safety and efficacy data

• Analyze, evaluate, interpret, and report clinical data

• Anticipate and solve complex drug development problems

• Contribute to regulatory strategy

• Contribute to drafting and reviewing of clinical documents, manuscripts, presentations, and regulatory submissions

• Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant science, medical information, good clinical practices, and regulatory guidance

• Collaborate with—and serve as a clinical research resource for—cross-functional colleagues (e.g. in clinical operations, statistics, regulatory affairs, medical affairs, health economics outcomes research, commercial, finance) to optimize product development

• Contribute to (and may be asked to represent the clinical development department in) corporate strategic and organizational initiatives

• Cultivate relationships with investigative sites, clinical consultants, and key opinion leaders to represent the interests of the company

• Assist in portfolio management and commercial activities as needed

• Complete assigned tasks thoroughly, accurately, and on time

• Adhere to rigorous ethical standards

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold an M.D. degree and preferably also a Ph.D. degree. You have hands-on experience treating patients.

Furthermore, you have:

• At least 5-7 years of industry experience (other relevant experience e.g., post-graduate experience in the clinical and/or academic realms may also be considered on a case-by-case basis).

• Strong track record of scientific and clinical inquiry

• Possess excellent communication skills (written and oral)

• Demonstrate sound judgement in terms of handling complex, confidential, and regulated information

Key competencies:

You have a proven ability to learn quickly, even in fast‑paced environments.

You take ownership of your work, lead by example, and collaborate effectively with colleagues across the organization. You are trusted by others for your sound judgment and discretion, particularly when handling confidential, sensitive, or regulated information.

To succeed in the position, we expect you to be comfortable working with complex instructions, managing multiple priorities, and consistently maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.

Travel: 20-30 days per year

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation. Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed. If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

jobs.description:
Drive Market Readiness for the Next Generations of Hearing Solutions

At Demant Hearing Aids, we are transforming how we bring innovation to market through our new Product-to-Success (P2S) framework. As a global organization with a strong cadence of product launches, our competitiveness depends on turning innovation into meaningful value for our customers and users.

We are looking for a commercially minded and highly collaborative Project Director, Commercial Market Readiness. This is a new role in which you will bring the voice of the markets into global product development and launch planning. You will also ensure that global plans are translated into market-ready execution, so our innovations deliver successful commercial outcomes.

As a key member of the Program Management Team (PMT), you will lead Market Readiness deliveries across Marketing, Sales, Training, and Service. Your objective is to ensure that the commercial organization is fully prepared to launch new products successfully.

This role sits at the intersection of commercial strategy, program execution, and cross-functional leadership. You will connect activities across the Growth Engine (Global Marketing) and Revenue Engine (Global Sales), creating alignment and ensuring coordinated execution. We are recruiting two new Market Readiness colleagues for this role, who will alternate lead responsibility across releases, giving each release one clear Market Readiness lead (internally referred to as NMRI). The roles will report to the respective commercial leaders in Marketing and Sales.

Experience from a market organization, sales company, or another market-facing role will be a strong advantage, giving you valuable insight into customer needs, commercial execution, product adoption, and market impact.

Your Responsibilities

As our Commercial Market Readiness Lead, you will:

Lead Market Readiness in the Program Management Team

• Communicate global strategies and launch plans ensuring locally executable plans and launch readiness across markets.

• Champion market needs and launch realities within the program, ensuring decisions reflect the perspectives of customers and users, hearing care professionals and sales companies.

• Represent Market Readiness in the PMT and ensure timely, high-quality delivery against agreed milestones.

• Coordinate cross-functional activities and provide clear visibility of progress, risks, dependencies, quality, compliance, and overall readiness.

• Enable confident and timely decisions through concise status reporting, clear recommendations, and early escalation of critical issues.

Act as a Commercial and Strategic Leader

• Ensure market readiness activities align with broader business objectives and commercial ambitions.

• Drive collaboration across global and local functions, ensuring market perspectives influence key program decisions and that solutions are practical, scalable, and relevant for local execution.

• Translate market insights and commercial realities into actionable recommendations for the program and leadership teams.

What You Bring

We are looking for an experienced leader who combines strong commercial understanding and market understanding with excellent project and stakeholder management capabilities. As this is a new role, you will have a unique opportunity to shape and establish it together with colleagues across the global and local value chain.

Experience

• First-hand experience in a market-facing role or in close partnership with sales companies, with the ability to bring an outside-in perspective to program decisions.

• Significant experience in commercial project leadership, product launches, market readiness, or a related field.

• Proven ability to navigate complex stakeholder landscapes and influence without direct authority.

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in business or a related field, combined with at least five years of experience in sales, marketing, project management, or another commercial environment.

Competencies

• Lead with a strong business and commercial mindset.

• Create clarity, alignment, and momentum across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Drive predictability and transparency through disciplined planning and execution.

• Practice structured, timely, and effective communication.

• Build trust and collaboration across functions and organizational levels.

How to apply

If you thrive in a dynamic environment where commercial impact, stakeholder leadership, and program excellence come together, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please submit your CV and a short motivation letter via our online application portal no later than November 22nd, 2026.

For further information about the position, please contact Dorthe Krogh Jensen, Vice President, Brand Management, at djen@demant.com or Steven Schmidt, Head of Global Sales at stns@demant.com

We expect to conduct first-round interviews during weeks 48-49, with second-round interviews taking place in week 50.

Join us and help turn innovation into market success.

At Demant, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnicity, age, gender, personality, disability, or educational background. Diversity is an integral part of our culture, and we particularly encourage women pursuing careers in STEM to apply, supporting United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5: Gender Equality.

Demant is a world-leading hearing healthcare and technology group built on a heritage of care, health, and innovation since 1904. The Group offers innovative technologies, solutions, and expertise to help people hear better. In every aspect, from hearing care, hearing aids and hearing implants to diagnostic equipment and services and audio solutions, Demant is active and engaged. Are you passionate about shaping a more sustainable future and would you like to play a key role in Vattenfall’s transition to cleaner energy? Do you want to help drive the development, construction, and operation of our offshore wind portfolio? Vattenfall is looking for a Senior Consent Manager to strengthen its Offshore Consenting team in Denmark.

The Offshore Consenting team is an international team with representation in all Vattenfall’s key markets. We are involved throughout the offshore wind value chain, from pre-tender, through the tendering phase, project delivery, and throughout the operational phase. We are responsible for securing permits for Vattenfall’s offshore wind portfolio, and for enabling permit compliance during project delivery and operations.

In Denmark, Vattenfall and its partners are operating 5 offshore wind farms, including the Vesterhav Nord and Syd projects that were fully commissioned in 2024. Beyond our current portfolio, we have been awarded the two new Danish projects Hesselø and North Sea Central both including an onshore and offshore scope.

**What will you do?

**As Senior Consent Manager, you will play a pivotal role in enabling our offshore wind projects in Denmark. You will act as a coordinator and problem solver within the organization, working together with different teams and disciplines. In addition, you will be a key contact person externally towards authorities. For this position we are looking for a candidate with a strong profile within onshore permitting and environmental conditions, e.g., experience from onshore grid infrastructure projects in Denmark.

**

• Analyse Consenting requirements, risks, and opportunities to support project execution

• Deliver and implement a Consenting Strategy in development and construction of the projects in collaboration with the offshore scope.

• Ensure timely application for and receipt of permits, licenses and dispensations

• Work with project teams and packages to enable full permit compliance of their respective scopes;

• Engage with and report to both local and state authorities.

• Monitor and anticipate regulatory developments with a potential impact on our permits.

**Location

**Qualifications

**You have an analytical mindset coupled with strong project management, communication- and interpersonal skills. You can structure and process complex information and discern implications for our business and can communicate clearly with various stakeholders and secure quality and timelines in projects.

You have experience working in international and multidisciplinary teams and thrive in a dynamic environment, skillfully managing multiple tasks under tight deadlines. Your excellent interpersonal, communication, and stakeholder management skills allow you to build and maintain positive relationships across diverse teams. You can work well independently and in collaboration with others and have the dedication to see a task through despite challenges. Above all, you consistently prioritize health and safety in all aspects of your work.

You can have fun whilst being serious and are serious about having fun.

**

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in the fields of biology, environmental science, spatial planning, or another relevant field;

• Knowledge of onshore environmental and spatial planning regulations;

• Ideally you have +5 years of relevant experience. Alternatively, you have gained (permit management) experience in other renewable energy, or other large infrastructure-, industrial-, or construction projects;

• Excellent oral and written communication skills in Danish (native or near native) and English (full working proficiency).

jobs.description:
Would you like the freedom to shape how colleagues across countries, functions and teams connect with the bigger picture? Do you love finding the story behind the message and turning complex topics into communication people actually want to read?

Help shape the future of internal communication at ABENA – starting with the platform that brings us together.

At ABENA, we are strengthening our People & Culture agenda, with an ambition to create an even better employee experience across our organization. Our focus on job satisfaction, engagement and a strong sense of belonging also means continuously developing how we connect and communicate with our colleagues.

We are looking to rethink our internal communication platform and move toward a modern Microsoft 365 environment. You will play a central role i rethinking how colleagues across countries, functions and teams find information, share stories and connect with the bigger picture through our future internal communication platform.

As our new Global Internal Communication & Engagement Specialist, you will step into a newly created role with considerable freedom to shape both the role and how we communicate across ABENA. If you see a better way to communicate, we want to hear it. You will create content yourself, turn business priorities and leadership messages into clear and engaging communication, and find stories worth sharing across functions and countries.

The aim is to do more than keep people informed: bring colleagues closer to our business, create engagement and strengthen the feeling of being part of one ABENA.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Create engaging internal content - write and shape global news, leadership communication, town hall content and stories that engages all employees.

• Help shape our future digital workplace – bring the business and communication perspective as we rethink our internal communication platform and move toward a modern Microsoft 365 environment.

• Own and set direction for how we communicate internally – help define principles, formats and communication flows, including what we communicate, where and how.

• Bring stories to life across ABENA – spot good stories across countries and functions, work with local editors and turn input into communication people want to read.

• Guide and spar with colleagues responsible for local communication, helping them apply best practices, turn local input into engaging content, and creating greater consistency between global and local communication.

• Keep communication relevant and moving – plan communication activities and editorial calendars, follow up on execution and use feedback and insights to continuously improve how we communicate.

What we are looking for:

• 3–5 years of experience in internal, corporate or organizational communication, ideally from an international organization with multiple countries and stakeholders.

• A digitally curious and tech-savvy communicator with a good understanding of internal communication and engagement platforms and their possibilities. Experience with SharePoint, Microsoft 365, or similar environments is a strong advantage.

• A strong writer and content creator who knows how to find the story, sharpen the message and adapt communication to different audiences and channels.

• Experience turning leadership decisions, organizational changes and complex topics into communication that is simple, relevant and easy to understand.

• The confidence to set direction and create structure – you are comfortable establishing formats, guidelines and ways of working and helping others apply them consistently.

• A hands-on and outgoing approach – you enjoy reaching out across the organization, building relationships and getting things from idea to finished communication, while keeping track of many moving parts.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in Danish and English.

Your Team, Our Culture and Values

You will join our Group HR team, working alongside experienced HR specialists and generalists who work closely together, share ideas, and use each other’s different perspectives and expertise. Even when things are busy, we make room for laughter and a good atmosphere. We value collaboration and openness. For us, it is important that we support one another, and that it is genuinely enjoyable to come to work. Creating and maintaining a positive atmosphere and a great team spirit is something we are all responsible for.

Your leader at ABENA will be Lotte Blanner, HR Director, who describes her leadership style as follows:

“Trust and clear direction. I actively seek and value your input in our shared work, and I listen to your ambitions so I can support both your tasks and your development through honest feedback and clear priorities. I value people who take ownership and show initiative. You can count on me to stand by you and back you up along the way. We aim high but set realistic ambitions and take a pragmatic approach to the realities we work within.”

At ABENA, you become part of a global company with a clear purpose: making a real difference in people’s everyday lives. Across the organization, we are guided by three core values: Trust, Fairness, and Cooperation. They shape how we work together, make decisions, and take responsibility for moving ABENA forward.

We look forward to hearing from you and receiving your application.

If you are interested in the position, please send your CV as soon as possible. We review applications as we receive them and will close the search once we have found our new colleague.

Read more about our recruitment process here.

If you would like to know more about the role, feel free to contact Group HR Consultant Kári Thorsson at +45 5158 1917.

**Description

**At Factbird, we're redefining how manufacturing runs. By combining hardware, firmware, cloud, and AI, we turn raw production data into real, measurable impact on factory floors around the world. This is a product built by and for people who understand what happens on the shop floor. We’re on a mission to make it easier and faster for manufacturers to work smarter to increase productivity and eliminate waste.

For this mission we're building fast, scaling with purpose, and solving problems that matter. Now, we're looking for an addition to our product management team, who want to bring our product into the future by expanding upon how we create real value on the factory floor.

The position product management plays at Factbird is both high-impact and also hands-on. As a product manager here, you’ll set direction, own the roadmap, and drive execution from idea to launch and beyond. You’ll play a key role in shaping how our platform scales and how our customers succeed.

**

About the role

**You’ll work closely with a dedicated development team and your peer product leaders, and you report to the Director of Product.

Production Insights: As a key platform application the candidate requires a strong PM backbone with a focus on having built products that communicate complex datasets and provide actionable insights to different user groups. To succeed in this role, previous experience from manufacturing industries is a key differentiator for us. Whether you have stood on that shopfloor and owned its numbers yourself or have worked for manufacturing and know exactly what "real value" means to the people running a production line – we take “knowing our customers” very serious for this particular position.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Turn strategy into shipped products: Define roadmaps, prioritize ruthlessly, and work closely with stakeholders to ensure we solve the biggest problems our customers are facing.

• Lead across disciplines: Act as the glue between product, firmware, cloud, UX, and business stakeholders - making sure everyone is aligned, focused, and moving fast.

• Identify signals in noise: Clarify customer needs, outline their jobs to be done and translate findings into clear and concise user stories.

• Spearhead continuous discovery: Build and maintain strong relationships with both internal and external stakeholders to gather key insights.

• Launch, learn, iterate: Drive product launches, gather customer feedback, and continuously evolve features based on real-world usage.

• Own performance & outcomes: Define and track key performance metrics aligned with product objectives.

**About you

**You have experienced first-hand how a shop floor is operated to ensure targets are met and continuous improvements are realized. You thrive in environments where ownership is high, pace is fast, and impact is visible. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information and love turning complexity into clarity, because you've had to do exactly that on a production floor before.

You are curious about technology and are keen to figure out what it enables for people who live and breathe shop floor realities every day. You care deeply about understanding the underlying problem before working on a solution. You want to build products that drive real value, something customers depend on, not just move on to the next shiny thing.

**

Requirements**

• Solid Product Management Experience: You are well-versed in product management frameworks and agile processes and can bring them into play with a practical approach, leveraging frameworks where they create clarity, structure, and speed.

• You've worked hands-on on the shopfloor for a while. You've been accountable for ensuring performance meets expectations by collaborating with the likes of operators, process engineers, continuous improvement leads, and plant or operations managers. This operational depth is what lets you translate real production pain into product decisions, and it is a hard requirement for this specific role — without it, the rest of the role is very difficult to do well. Our products play an essential role in manufacturing operations, and your experience within this field is essential.

• A continuous discovery mindset: You talk to customers constantly, map their jobs to be done, and identify commonalities. You're comfortable sitting with ambiguity until the real problem surfaces.

• Strong data and analytics instinct: Comfortable working with data and understanding how to turn analysis into concrete actions.

• A natural communicator: You speak the language of engineers, designers, operators, and leadership alike, adapting how you communicate to whoever's in the room.

• Driving teams: Proven ability to set and agree direction and goals with R&D teams, driving the team and getting to results in a manner where the team feels proud of the outcome.

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.
